relevance_note: Retrospective series of four children with genetically confirmed HA20: 'Whole-exome sequencing identified heterozygous TNFAIP3 (NM_006290.4) mutations or deletion in all patients'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON, cutting table spans from the paper's own table lines (row label through the patient's cell) and checking every span verbatim. Tables 1-3 have patients as columns, headers 'Patient 1'..'Patient 4' (data columns 1-4). Table 1 legend defines '−' as Negative (used as excluded with the legend quoted); Table 2 legend defines '−' as Normal, bold as abnormal and '/' as not done ('/' cells recorded as nothing). Non-bold numeric lab values (e.g. ESR 19 for Patient 3, HGB 110 for Patient 4) were not turned into excluded rows; directions for bold ALB/NE/LDH values (low/low/elevated) were read against the printed reference range. No stacked ' / ' cells. Parents: the paper describes both parents of Patients 1, 3 and 4 as tested wild-type (Fig. 1C, 3B, 4C), so each gets a row ('parent of Patient n', sex not stated); Patient 2's parents are not described, so no rows. Contradictions: (1) Patient 4's variant is c.1243_1247del in the abstract, results text, ACMG sentence and Fig. 4 legend but c.1247_1251del in Table 3 (same protein p.Asn416Thrfs*11); the text form was recorded. (2) Text says 'Autoantibody panels, rheumatoid factor, skin prick test and pathogen screening were negative' but Table 2 shows 'RF-IgA elevated' for Patients 1, 2 and 4; RF-IgA rows were kept as observed from the table, no RF-negative rows were emitted from the unnamed text statement, and the 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' checklist item is not reported for Patients 1, 2 and 4. (3) Text says all four patients had anemia, but Patient 4's HGB (110, range 110-150) is not bold; anemia for Patient 4 recorded only from the group statement. (4) Abstract says lymphadenopathy 'in one case' but Table 2 shows lymph node enlargement for Patient 1 (CT) and Patient 4 (ultrasound); both recorded. (5) 'Patients 1, 3, and 4 carried novel frameshift or nonsense mutations' vs Patient 3's c.133C > T 'has been previously reported [5, 6]'; pathogenicity for Patient 3 recorded as 'pathogenic' only. (6) Table 2 lists P1 'CD8 + T cells increased; B cells decreased' while the Discussion says 'T/B lymphopenia in Patients 1 and 2'; both recorded. Patient 2 inheritance: Table 3 says 'de novo', but the paper states parental testing (absent in both parents) only for c.866delA, c.133C > T and c.1243_1247del, so Patient 2's inheritance is 'not reported' under rule 8. Abstract statements about unnamed patients ('1 patient ... still had intermittent fever and perianal aphthosis'; 'One patient ... repeated hospitalizations for recurrent infections') were not assigned to individuals. 'Arthritis −' for Patients 1, 3, 4 does not exclude 'arthritis or arthralgia'; 'Skin eruption −' was taken to exclude the skin-lesions checklist item, 'Oculopathy −' the ocular item, 'Hepatic injury −' autoimmune hepatitis (Patients 1-3). Gastroscopy '−' recorded as 'abnormal gastroscopy' excluded (whole investigation, D-27). The paper does not say Patient 3 was described earlier, although ref [6] (Liu P, Wang YS et al., 2020, infantile-onset IBD with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 mutation) is cited for the same variant and shares a surname/initials with the senior author; cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null.
